sources.sweepMetres: The blade sculls just ahead of her bow, about 0.3 m beyond her 0.69 m half-width: 1 m from her middle
sources.handsAboveWaterMetres: Her seat lies about her waterline, and a seated man's shoulders stand about 0.6 m over his seat (NASA-STD-3000, sitting shoulder height of a 50th-percentile man, 0.59 m)
sources.bowDrag: Round, so the same from every side as across her
sources.sideDrag: A short upright cylinder in cross-flow, mirrored at the surface into one twice her draft, has a drag coefficient of about 0.6 on diameter by height (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3); a bowl's rounded bottom sheds less, as a sphere's 0.47 on its frontal area does

sources.parts: By the model (bin/lib/hulls/coracle.py): 2.12 m² of hide 5 mm thick at 860 kg/m³, 9.1 kg, over 14 lattice laths and three plaits of 1 by 6 cm, 33 m of willow, 8 kg: 17 kg, as Hornell (1938) gives one-man coracles at 18 to 40 lb
sources.swimmingOffsetY: Drawn at the draft she floats at with one aboard, 0.086 m (bin/lib/hulls/coracle.py): vanilla floats a boat with the water 0.018 m over her selection box's top less this offset
sources.shell: Raw cowhide is 2 to 6 mm thick. A blow springs back off the hide unless a lath backs it where it lands: by the model, the lattice's 14 laths 6 cm wide cross 65% of the bottom, and their 28 ends rising to the gunwale 47% of the sides. A breaker presses the hide onto them, each lath 1 cm deep bending over the 0.37 m from the bottom to the gunwale
sources.depthMetres: Bottom to gunwale: the laths rise 0.35 m (Museum Wales, Teifi coracle), as the model draws them
sources.waterplaneSquareMetres: So that her 265 L bowl full, with one aboard, brings her gunwale to the water (bin/lib/hulls/physics.py)
sources.seep: A seam where one hide meets the next weeps once the fat has washed out of it: some 1.8 m of seam across her bowl, weeping as the currach's do a metre. A coracle from before her build is covered in prepared hide over her two sections, with no seam, as her old recipe's one large hide had
sources.cover: The hides a vessel is covered with as her build lays them; one from before her build is covered with prepared hides, as the grid made her

sources.heave: A 17 kg basket sits on the water and rises with the crest
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: A crest that catches the low rim tips the bowl and its paddler out: coracles keep to rivers and sheltered water
sources.rollResponse: A round, flat bowl tilts with every slope of the water
sources.pitchResponse: Round, it tilts the same every way

sources.capacityLitres: Her bowl inside the hide and laths, to the gunwale, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/coracle.py)
sources.deckSquareMetres: Her mouth inside the gunwale, by the model (bin/lib/hulls/coracle.py)

sources.time: A held action lasts the real time of that one piece of work over sixty: game time runs 30 times faster than real time, and boat work is halved again
sources.layout: Teifi coracles were begun as a lattice of laths laid flat on the ground, seven along and seven across (Hornell 1938), their ends bent up later into the gunwale. Spaced as her model draws them (ALONG_SPACING and ACROSS_SPACING in bin/lib/hulls/coracle.py), whole steps of the 1/16 m the bed lays laths by, so a lath laid on its place stays there when she is bound; one laid a step off is moved that step
sources.binding: One rope ties a dozen crossings of the bottom, a few turns of cord each, some quarter of an hour (an estimate); the shape's builder counts the crossings on her bottom
sources.gunwale: Plaiting one lath round the bent-up ends, some ten minutes (an estimate); Teifi gunwales were three plaits of soaked hazel (Hornell 1938). The laths dry in place and set her shape in a couple of days, as the canoe's ribs do
sources.cover: Stretching and sewing a small hide's worth of cover, some twenty minutes (an estimate); a bigger hide covers more at once and takes as much longer
sources.lacing: The hide laced to the gunwale at short intervals (Hornell 1938), every 5 cm, each turn round the gunwale and the hide's edge: the shape's builder counts the rope
sources.framePart: Her frame is the wood of her laths: its share and the weight it was set for are willow's, its strength and density are those of the wood split
